segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hello, I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil. And this is Real Easy English,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: the podcast with real conversations in easy English to help you learn.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: If you want to read along with this podcast,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: you can find a text version on our website.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Visit bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hi Beth, how are things this week?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Things are good, Neil. How are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you very much. Today we're talking all about cooking.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We'll talk about what we like to cook as well as our favourite recipes.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Recipes. Can you explain the word recipes, Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, a recipe is a list of instructions

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: for how to make certain types of food.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, great. Let's get started then.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, Neil, do you enjoy cooking?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes I do enjoy cooking When I cook I find it relaxing How about you

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah I the same I cook quite a lot but I really enjoy it when I can be in the kitchen

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: with music or a podcast on and really relax and spend time making food.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What's your favourite thing to make?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I quite like making stir fries because they're quick and easy. There's lots of different ingredients and flavours you can use. But I also quite like cooking fish. I've got some good fish recipes.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Ah, OK.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I like to cook a roast dinner.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Very British.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, on a Sunday. Let me tell you how to do roast chicken.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK, give me the recipe.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK. Take a chicken and put garlic and rosemary and lemons inside.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Then boil some potatoes, not too long,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and put everything in the oven

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and roast it with some vegetables for about an hour and 15 minutes

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Mmm sounds really good

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, Beth, I want to hear about your fish recipe.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, there's one I like which is with cod.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, you put the cod in a pan with stock, creme fraiche and tarragon.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: That's it. It's really simple.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: There's only four ingredients, but it tastes really delicious.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Sounds amazing.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: How does your chicken recipe taste,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Neil?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It tastes fantastic, I have to say.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I think especially because of the gravy,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: and the gravy is a sauce made from all of the juices from the chicken and the vegetables.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I love gravy.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I use gravy on my bangers and mash.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Bangers and mash? What's that?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bangers and mash is another British recipe,

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: which is sausages and mashed potato.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: The sausages are the bangers and the mash is the mashed potato

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Mmm I can almost smell it

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I know I getting hungry

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Let's look at the language we learnt during the conversation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We had recipe, the instructions for cooking a particular food or meal.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Taste, which we use to describe the food we eat.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For example, my chicken tastes amazing.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And Neil, you gave me instructions on how to make that delicious roast chicken and you used the imperative.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: You said put lemon, garlic and herbs in the chicken, boil the potatoes, but not for too long, and add them to the dish.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: That's it for this episode of Real Easy English.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: For more on the imperative and other grammar tips, try our podcast Learning English Grammar.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: You can find it on your podcast app or by visiting our website bbclearningenglish.com.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Next time, we'll talk more about our families and the jobs they do.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: See you then. Goodbye.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Bye.
